# AI, FICO & the Next Big Risks in Financial Services

First listed: 2026-10-21 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [Substack: AI, FICO & the Next Big Risks in Financial Services](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/ai-fico-and-the-next-big-risks-in) - 2026-10-21

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Eisman and Collins survey FICO competition, AI risks to insurance and idle cash, payment networks, bank mergers, software refinancing, rates, life insurers and crypto regulation. Eisman explicitly endorses several concerns in his closing summary. FHFA verifies pricing parity; Senate records verify CLARITY's procedural defeat. The claim that no direct-lending index exists is incorrect. Eisman's leveraged-equity arithmetic is valid under fixed-debt assumptions, while the broad software markdown premise is unverified and the refinancing forecast is still ahead.

The episode has many separable theses, with conditional AI risks and refinancing arithmetic distinct from observed outcomes. Recording date is September 30, three weeks before publication. Permanently dead legislation is not established by one failed vote.

<a id="substack-220412338-c032"></a>
### 032. If a company bought with 50% debt loses half its enterprise value while debt remains unchanged, its residual equity value is wiped out.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | supporting

[Source at 26:20-26:27](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/ai-fico-and-the-next-big-risks-in) | Stance: conditional | Horizon: not stated

Let initial EV be 100 and net debt 50; after EV falls to 50, residual equity is zero. This does not verify the real-world premises.

Conditional reasoning: Equity=max(EV-net debt,0). Initial EV=100 and debt=50; a 50% EV decline leaves EV=50 and debt=50, so equity=0. Assumes no debt amortization, retained cash, additional assets or option value.

Assessment test: Apply equity = enterprise value minus net debt under the stated fixed-debt assumptions.
